text: Alpine cheeses are scalded hot and ripened for months in large wheels. Emmental-type cheeses are also given propionic bacteria and a spell in a warm room, where the gas they make grows the eyes; Gruyère-type cheeses stay in a cool cellar and are smeared, and have few eyes or none.
